name: YouTube
tagline: World's largest video platform: long-form, Shorts, TV, music and live
facts: Largest user market; Shorts filled TikTok ban gap

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Give everyone a voice and show them the world.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Be the default screen for all video, from 15-second Shorts to living-room TV and live sports.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Two-sided flywheel: share ~55% of ad revenue with creators, attract more content, more watch time, more advertisers.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Largest creator library, Google ad stack, search intent data, recommendation engine and Content ID rights system.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Connected TV plus subscriptions; Premium, Music and NFL Sunday Ticket now growing faster than ads.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Shorts monetises below long-form per hour; is Shorts cannibalising YouTube's most valuable watch time?

customers.pain: Endless choice, need free entertainment, learning and music on any screen
customers.why: Deepest catalogue anywhere, free with ads, great recommendations, works on phone and TV

customers.who: Partners from hobbyists to media studios
customers.pain: Need audience, predictable income and tools to grow
customers.why: Partner Program revenue share, global reach, evergreen search traffic, multiple monetisation levers

customers.pain: Reach cord-cutters and Gen Z with measurable outcomes
customers.why: Google Ads targeting, CTV reach rivalling TV networks, Demand Gen and shoppable ads

customers.pain: Ads interrupt, need offline and background play
customers.why: Premium removes ads and bundles YouTube Music; cheaper than separate services

customers.pain: Piracy and fragmented distribution of their content
customers.why: Content ID monetises user uploads; huge reach for licensed and live content

rows.who_uses: All free viewers on mobile, web and TV
rows.who_pays: Advertisers via Google Ads and DV360
rows.how: CPM/CPV auctions; creators get ~55% long-form, 45% Shorts pool
Subscription fee; share paid to creators and labels by watch time
Resells network channels; thin margins due to carriage fees

rows.who_uses: Fans of specific creators or networks
rows.how: YouTube takes a platform cut, typically ~30%

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: 2025: ~$40B ads (67%) and ~$20B subscriptions (33%); subscriptions growing faster than ads in 2026.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Billions watch free; ~125M pay for Music/Premium, so most users monetised through ads only.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: No content production cost; creators paid revenue share, so margins scale; TV bundle is low-margin.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Shorts monetisation, CTV ad pricing, Premium price/Lite tier, shopping, sports rights, AI dubbing for global reach.

bullets.label: Lesson
bullets.text: Revenue-share model turns creators into an unpaid-upfront content studio; ad business funds the flywheel.

friction: Rising ad load and unskippable ads frustrate free users
Shorts feed interrupts long-form intent on home page
Creator demonetisation and opaque policy strikes
Premium price hikes feel steep in emerging markets

competitors.label: Edge

competitors.label: Risk
competitors.text: TikTok attention share, AI slop, regulation on minors and content moderation
